before.label: Sparse and sliding-window attention
before.definition: Attention restricted to local windows or fixed sparse patterns so cost grows linearly rather than quadratically with sequence length.

fields.definition: Attention restricted to local windows or predetermined sparse patterns, reducing attended query-key pairs; cost is linear in sequence length when the attended positions per query remain bounded.

changes.rationale: Fixed sparse patterns do not necessarily have linear attention cost; bounded attended positions per query justify the narrower linear-cost statement.

sources.supports: Sparse Transformers uses sparse factorizations with O(n sqrt(n)) complexity, providing a counterexample to the universal linear-cost claim.

before.predicate: makes long contexts affordable by linearizing attention cost over
before.conditions: Positions attend only within a window or fixed sparse pattern, possibly at a quality cost on long-range tasks.

fields.predicate: makes longer contexts more affordable by reducing attention cost over
fields.conditions: The attention pattern reduces attended query-key pairs relative to dense attention; linear cost requires bounded attended positions per query, and quality on long-range tasks may change.

changes.rationale: Fixed sparse patterns do not necessarily have linear attention cost; bounded attended positions per query justify the narrower linear-cost statement.

sources.supports: Sparse Transformers uses sparse factorizations with O(n sqrt(n)) complexity, providing a counterexample to the universal linear-cost claim.
